data.title: Provider
data.tagline: A platform or infrastructure entity that hosts, runs, and serves large language models through APIs.
data.learningOutcome: You can use the Provider, Model, Base URL, and API key source in a configuration to identify who provides the service.
data.description: A model vendor, cloud platform, aggregation gateway, or even a local model service may appear as a Provider in a tool. It receives requests and provides model access, often handling credentials, rate limits, or billing, but it does not necessarily train or directly run the underlying model. Check the Base URL, key issuer, and billing party to identify the actual path.

learning.assumes: You have used an AI tool that returns an answer or code.
learning.outcome: You can use the Provider, Model, Base URL, and API key source in a configuration to identify who provides the service.

distinctions.label: API Proxy
distinctions.explanation: A Provider is the entity hosting model weights, inference compute, and billing; an API Proxy is an intermediary forwarding traffic between the client and provider.

explanation.title: Use a chef to understand a Provider
explanation.text: Imagine you are looking for a chef to cook a dish: the Model is the chef who actually cooks, the Provider is the restaurant or platform that provides the chef and service, the API is the counter where you place an order, the API Key is the membership card that proves you are allowed to order, and the Base URL is the restaurant's address. So, the Provider is who you use to access an AI model.

explanation.title: What do Provider and Model mean in a configuration?
explanation.text: `provider: openai` with `model: gpt-5` means using gpt-5 through OpenAI. `provider: deepseek` with `model: deepseek-chat` means using deepseek-chat through DeepSeek. In short: the Provider is who supplies the service, and the Model is which model you select. If the configured Provider is `openai-compatible`, it usually means that the service platform accepts a request format similar to OpenAI. It does not prove that the request goes to OpenAI; check the Base URL, key issuer, and billing party to identify the actual service platform.

data.boundary: Even with the same Model, Providers may differ in price, speed, stability, context limits, image or tool-call support, and data handling. Read four settings together: Provider is who you call through, Model is what you select, Base URL is where the request goes, and API key identifies the credential issuer.

lessonPractice.title: provider: OpenRouter, model: deepseek-v4-flash. Who is the model provider we connect to?

options.label: OpenRouter
options.feedback: Correct. Provider says which service platform you call, while Model says which model you select. The provider here is OpenRouter.

options.label: deepseek-v4-flash
options.feedback: That is the Model name, not the Provider. It identifies which model is selected, not which service platform receives the request.

options.label: It cannot be determined
options.feedback: The configuration explicitly says `provider: OpenRouter`, so the request goes through OpenRouter.

data.agentPrompt: Check whether the configured Provider, Model, Base URL, and API key source agree. First report where the request goes, who issued the credential, and who bills it; do not read or print the real API key or change the configuration.
